newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Japan non-banks apply for special liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Two Japan non-banks apply for special liquidation.

text.p: Non-bank financial companies Sanwa Tatemono Sogo Finance Co Ltd and CS Sogo Service Kabushiki Kaisha applied on Thursday for special liquidation at the Tokyo District Court, the firms' lawyers said.
Sanwa's debts totalled 66.45 billion yen and CS's debts totalled 71.3 billion yen, the lawyers said.
The court declined to confirm the applications.
Sanwa was formed in 1986 as a subsidiary of Sanwa Tatemono Co Ltd to provide loans for real estate businesses, private research company Teikoku Databank Ltd said in its report.

In February 1994, the parent company, which was a real estate developer, filed for court protection from creditors with outstanding debts totalling about 124.3 billion yen, making it difficult for the unit to recover loans to its parent company of about 58 billion yen, Teikoku said.

CS Sogo was formed in 1986 as a wholly owned subsidiary of one of Japan's "jusen" mortgage firms to conduct real estate and financial businesses, Teikoku said in another report. The mortgage firm has since failed.
CS Sogo's problem loans increased due to the collapse of the so-called "bubble" economy of inflated share and property prices, Teikoku said.
